sections.title: Angles and Measurement
sections.content: Angles are measured in Degrees or Radians. The conversion formula is: π radians = 180°. Therefore, 1 radian = 180/π degrees, and 1 degree = π/180 radians. Arc length l = rθ (where θ is in radians).

sections.title: Basic Trigonometric Ratios
sections.content: In a right-angled triangle: sinθ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse, cosθ = Base/Hypotenuse, tanθ = Perpendicular/Base. The reciprocals are cscθ, secθ, and cotθ respectively.

sections.title: Fundamental Identities
sections.content: The three core Pythagorean identities are: 1) sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 2) 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 3) 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ. These are valid for all values of θ where the functions are defined.

sections.title: Signs of Trigonometric Functions (ASTC Rule)
sections.content: The coordinate plane is divided into 4 quadrants. ASTC Rule: Q1 = All positive, Q2 = Sine & Cosec positive, Q3 = Tan & Cot positive, Q4 = Cos & Sec positive.

sections.title: Allied Angles
sections.content: Formulas for angles like (90°±θ), (180°±θ), etc. If the angle involves 90° or 270° (odd multiples of π/2), the function changes to its co-function (sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot, sec ↔ csc). For 180° or 360°, the function remains the same. The sign is determined by the ASTC rule.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Forgetting to change the function (sin to cos) when dealing with (90±θ) or (270±θ).
2) Applying the wrong sign in the ASTC rule.
3) Using degrees in the arc length formula (l=rθ) instead of radians.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 is about the foundational definitions of trigonometry: knowing your right triangle ratios, memorizing standard values, applying Pythagorean identities, and determining signs using ASTC.

tricks.title: ASTC Phrase
tricks.explanation: Remember the quadrants (1 to 4) using a simple acronym.
tricks.example: 'Add Sugar To Coffee' or 'All Sin Tan Cos' → Q1(All), Q2(Sin), Q3(Tan), Q4(Cos).

tricks.title: Value Substitution Trick
tricks.explanation: In objective questions asking to simplify a trigonometric expression, substitute a standard angle (like θ = 0°, 30°, or 45°) to quickly check options.
tricks.example: To simplify (secθ - tanθ)(secθ + tanθ), put θ=45°. (√2 - 1)(√2 + 1) = 2 - 1 = 1.

tricks.title: Sec and Tan Pair Trick
tricks.explanation: If secθ + tanθ = x, then secθ - tanθ = 1/x (and vice versa). The same applies to cscθ and cotθ.
tricks.example: If secθ + tanθ = 2, then secθ - tanθ = 1/2. Adding them gives 2secθ = 2.5.

tricks.title: Complementary Pairs
tricks.explanation: sin(x) = cos(90-x). If two angles A and B add up to 90°, then sin²A + sin²B = 1 and cos²A + cos²B = 1.

tricks.title: Hand/Finger Trick for Standard Values
tricks.explanation: Hold out your left hand. Assign 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 to fingers from thumb to pinky. For sinθ, count fingers below and use √(fingers)/2.
tricks.example: For sin(60°), index finger is 60. There are 3 fingers below it. Value = √3/2.

tricks.title: Pythagorean Triplets
tricks.explanation: Memorize common right triangle sides to bypass Pythagoras calculations completely.
